semantics: Every label the agentic-layer generator emits is listed here and scored. Gold that fails its own checksum (the invalid twins) stays scored, exactly as in the Kiji validator gold census; the per-label validity split is reported beside it and never replaces it. Layer A adjacent-address gold uses synthetic private-network host endpoints associated with a user's device. Documentation, loopback and link-local ranges are benign and scored as Layer D lookalikes instead. Layer D documents carry no gold, so every byte predicted there is a false positive. A label names a value even when it stands lines away, past a blank line, below the value, in a JSON key, sibling or nested field, or a CSV header: the labelled benign-lookalike cells of layer A are gold, and their layer D counterweights carry the same structures with no cue anywhere in the document. The address cells of layer A score every part of a whole address (house number, street, secondary unit or box, city, state, postcode) under its own label; the separators between parts are not gold, and a benign designator written beside an address (`test Suite 4`) is a recorded decoy, so covering it is a false positive. Their layer D counterweights carry the same designator words with no address anywhere. The phone-shape cells of layer A score a whole phone number, international prefix and parenthesised trunk zero included, in French dotted groups, national digit groups behind a phone label, `+CC (0)` and `00` / `001-` forms; their layer D counterweights carry dotted versions, dates and OIDs, firmware and part numbers written in the dotted phone shape, digit groups behind an order, invoice or ticket label, a signed score with a parenthesised zero, and `00`- or `001`-prefixed product, ticket, item and document codes (behind a spare country code or an unassignable NANP exchange when written in the phone's exact shape), with no phone label anywhere. Layer R decoys (words spelled like or containing a name part, digit runs shared with a repeated identifier) are not gold either, so a byte predicted over one is a false positive; every repeat of a real value is gold. An unlisted label fails closed, and so does a ruling on a label the generator no longer emits.

labels.label: BSN
labels.reason: Dutch citizen service number; generated checksum-valid with a checksum-invalid twin.

labels.label: BUILDINGNUM
labels.reason: House number, or a secondary unit or box written with its designator (`Suite 312`, `Apt. 771`, `Wohnung 4`, `3. Etage`, `PO Box 417`, `Postfach 505`, the `Box` of a US military address), inside a whole synthetic address. Scored per label until a composite ADDRESS entity exists; same label as layer C. A designator and number with no address in the document is benign.

labels.label: CITY
labels.reason: Invented city name inside a whole synthetic address, and the APO, FPO or DPO post office of a US military address, which stands where a city stands.

labels.label: CPF
labels.reason: Brazilian taxpayer number; generated checksum-valid with a checksum-invalid twin.

labels.label: CREDITCARDNUMBER
labels.reason: Payment card number; generated Luhn-valid with a Luhn-invalid twin.

labels.label: DATEOFBIRTH
labels.reason: Date of birth, with and without a cue; a date inserted as a birth date is personal data.

labels.label: EMAIL
labels.reason: Personal email address derived from a synthetic name.

labels.label: GIVENNAME
labels.reason: Given name of the sender in an email header or agent payload.

labels.label: IBAN
labels.reason: Personal bank account (DE, AT, NL, FR, GB); generated mod-97-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: IPADDRESS
labels.reason: Synthetic private-network host endpoint associated with a user's device; documentation, loopback and link-local addresses are benign.

labels.label: NHSNUMBER
labels.reason: UK NHS number; generated modulus-11-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: STATE
labels.reason: US state abbreviation between city and ZIP, and the AA, AE or AP code of a US military address. Kept in as in layer C; a state alone rarely identifies a person, so its place in the safety score needs an explicit ruling.

labels.label: STREET
labels.reason: Invented street name inside a whole synthetic address, and the PSC, CMR or Unit line of a US military address. Scored per label until a composite ADDRESS entity exists; same label as layer C.

labels.label: TAXNUM
labels.reason: German Steuer-ID; generated MOD 11,10-valid with an invalid twin.

labels.label: TELEPHONENUM
labels.reason: Personal phone number (German mobile, US). Includes a reserved-range phone (NANPA 555-01xx, German 01555) written as the tail of an ORDER- style reference when a label anywhere in the same document or record names it as a phone, in any language or script; the phone is gold, the reference word is not. A 16-digit run is never phone gold: no phone number has 16 digits. Includes a whole number in a documented fictional range (ARCEP fiction blocks, BNetzA media-production numbers, Ofcom drama numbers, NANPA 555-01xx) written as French dotted groups, with a parenthesised trunk zero after the country code, or behind a `00` or `001` international prefix, the prefix included; and national digit groups with no `+` behind a phone label, synthesized non-reachable (a leading 0 that the Spanish nine-digit and Danish eight-digit plans never use). The same digit groups with no phone label are benign.

labels.label: ZIPCODE
labels.reason: Synthetic postal code in an adjacent address field, including intentionally unassigned CA and GB shapes. Includes a five-digit US or German postcode written inside a benign-looking structure (the tail of an ORDER- style reference, or after a currency code) when a label anywhere in the same document or record names it as a postcode. Includes the postcode of a whole synthetic address: US ZIPs in the unassigned 000xx range, German PLZ in the unassigned 00xxx range and GB postcodes in the unused ZZ area.
